concept.name: Fractal indicator
concept.definition: Bill Williams' five-bar reversal marker: an up fractal is a series of at least five successive bars with the highest high in the middle and two lower highs on each side, and a down fractal is the mirror image with lows; one of the five indicators of his Trading Chaos system.
concept.intuition: A fractal flags a local extreme where the market pushed to a level and was rejected on both sides - a candidate swing point.
concept.mechanics: Mark an up arrow when the middle bar of five has the highest high with two lower highs on each side, and a down arrow symmetrically on lows. Because two bars must follow, the signal is confirmed only two bars late; Williams filtered fractals against the Alligator's Teeth line.
concept.formula: Up fractal at bar t: H_t > H_{t-1}, H_t > H_{t-2}, H_t > H_{t+1}, H_t > H_{t+2}; down fractal: L_t below the four surrounding lows.
concept.failure_modes: Five-bar fractals occur constantly and most are noise; the two-bar confirmation lag means entries come after part of the move, and counter-trend fractals fail repeatedly in trends.
concept.misconceptions: A fractal arrow is not a standalone trade signal - Williams used it as a level (entry on a break of the fractal) filtered by the Alligator, not as a reversal call by itself.
concept.example: Five bars with highs 10, 11, 12, 11, 10 put an up fractal on the middle bar (high 12), confirmed two bars later.
